settings.label: Secret key
settings.meaning: Authenticates the backend to Clerk's Backend API, which serves the instance's signing keys.
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Configure › API keys › Secret keys. The development instance has its own keys.

test.because: A development instance's secret key starts with sk_test_

production.because: A production instance's secret key starts with sk_live_

settings.label: Publishable key
settings.meaning: Names the instance, for the frontend and the SDK.
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Configure › API keys › Publishable key.

test.because: A development instance's publishable key starts with pk_test_

production.because: A production instance's publishable key starts with pk_live_

settings.label: JWT public key
settings.meaning: The instance's public key as PEM, to verify session tokens with no call to Clerk at all. Without it, the keys are read from the Backend API.
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Configure › API keys › Show JWT public key › PEM public key.

settings.label: Webhook signing secret
settings.meaning: Checks that a webhook came from Clerk (through Svix).
settings.whereToFind: Dashboard › Configure › Webhooks › the endpoint › Signing Secret (whsec_…).

operations.name: jwks.get
operations.purpose: Reads the instance's signing keys from the Backend API, without CLERK_JWT_KEY: when none are cached, every five minutes, and when a token names a key not yet seen (at most once every five seconds).

signature.description: Svix, which Standard Webhooks follows: svix-id, svix-timestamp (Unix seconds) and svix-signature headers; the signature is v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256 of '<id>.<timestamp>.<raw body>'> keyed with the base64 after whsec_. Several may be space-separated; one match is enough. Refuse a timestamp more than five minutes away.

events.meaning: A user signed up or was created.
A session ended (the user signed out).
A membership was changed (its role, say).
Clerk would send an email, and lets the app send it instead.
